```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

library(rio)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(kableExtra)
library(knitr)
library(scales)

options(scipen = 999)

# IMPORT DATA
W_SLUMS <- rio::import("../data/ddd3/SLUMS/W_SLUMS.xlsx")
W_VILLAGES<- rio::import("../data/ddd3/VILLAGES/W_VILLAGES.xlsx")

# DATA CLEANING
W_SLUMS <- W_SLUMS %>%
  rename(
    woman_index       = `_index`,
    slum_id           = Slum_ID,
    household_id      = Household_ID,
    joint_family      = Joint_family,
    fil_alive         = Father_in_law_alive,
    mil_alive         = Mother_in_law_alive,
    marital_status    = Marital_status,
    age               = Age,
    education         = Education,
    currently_working = Currently_Working
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    age           = ifelse(age == 0, NA, age),
    education     = ifelse(education > 16, NA, education),
    widow_sep     = ifelse(marital_status %in% c(3, 4), 1, 0),
    married       = as.integer(marital_status == 1),
    unmarried     = as.integer(marital_status == 2),
    joint_family  = as.integer(joint_family == 1),
    fil_alive     = as.integer(fil_alive == 1),
    mil_alive     = as.integer(mil_alive == 1),
    slum_id       = as.factor(slum_id),
    age_group = case_when(
      age >= 18 & age < 25 ~ 2,
      age >= 25 & age < 35 ~ 3,
      age >= 35 & age < 45 ~ 4,
      age >= 45 & age < 55 ~ 5,
      age >= 55 & age < 65 ~ 6,
      age >= 65            ~ 7
    ),
    edu_cat = case_when(
      education == 0                    ~ 1,
      education >= 1  & education <= 5  ~ 2,
      education >= 6  & education <= 8  ~ 3,
      education >= 9  & education <= 10 ~ 4,
      education >= 11 & education <= 12 ~ 5,
      education >= 13 & education <= 16 ~ 6
    ),
    age_18_24      = as.integer(age_group == 2),
    age_25_34      = as.integer(age_group == 3),
    age_35_44      = as.integer(age_group == 4),
    age_45_54      = as.integer(age_group == 5),
    age_55_64      = as.integer(age_group == 6),
    age_65plus     = as.integer(age_group == 7),
    edu_illiterate = as.integer(edu_cat == 1),
    edu_primary    = as.integer(edu_cat == 2),
    edu_middle     = as.integer(edu_cat == 3),
    edu_secondary  = as.integer(edu_cat == 4),
    edu_higher_sec = as.integer(edu_cat == 5),
    edu_graduate   = as.integer(edu_cat == 6)
  )

# SHARED THEME
theme_pres <- function() {
  theme_minimal(base_size = 28) +
    theme(
      plot.title      = element_text(face = "bold", size = 32,
                                     hjust = 0.5, margin = margin(b = 20)),
      axis.title      = element_text(size = 26),
      axis.text       = element_text(size = 24),
      legend.position = "none",
      plot.margin     = margin(20, 40, 20, 40)
    )
}
```

```{r}
#| label: functions
#| include: false

fmt  <- function(x, d = 2) ifelse(is.na(x), "",
          format(round(x, d), big.mark = ",", nsmall = d, trim = TRUE))
fmt0 <- function(x) ifelse(is.na(x), "",
          format(round(x, 0), big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE))

row_dummy <- function(label, var) {
  v <- W_SLUMS[[var]]
  v <- v[!is.na(v)]
  data.frame(
    Variable = paste0("&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;", label),
    N        = fmt0(length(v)),
    Mean     = fmt(mean(v), 3),
    SD       = fmt(sd(v), 3),
    Min      = "0",
    Max      = "1",
    panel    = "data",
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

panel_row <- function(label, type = "main") {
  data.frame(Variable = label, N = "", Mean = "", SD = "",
             Min = "", Max = "", panel = type,
             stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}

make_summary_table <- function() {
  rbind(
    panel_row("Panel A: Dependent Variable",               "main"),
    row_dummy("Currently Working (Yes = 1)",               "currently_working"),
    panel_row("Panel B: Independent Variables",            "main"),
    panel_row("&nbsp;&nbsp;Marital Status",                "sub"),
    row_dummy("Married (Yes = 1)",                         "married"),
    row_dummy("Unmarried (Yes = 1)",                       "unmarried"),
    row_dummy("Widowed / Separated (Yes = 1)",             "widow_sep"),
    panel_row("&nbsp;&nbsp;Family Structure",              "sub"),
    row_dummy("Joint Family (Yes = 1)",                    "joint_family"),
    panel_row("&nbsp;&nbsp;Age Groups",                    "sub"),
    row_dummy("Age 18&ndash;24",                           "age_18_24"),
    row_dummy("Age 25&ndash;34",                           "age_25_34"),
    row_dummy("Age 35&ndash;44 &nbsp;(ref)",               "age_35_44"),
    row_dummy("Age 45&ndash;54",                           "age_45_54"),
    row_dummy("Age 55&ndash;64",                           "age_55_64"),
    row_dummy("Age 65+",                                   "age_65plus"),
    panel_row("Panel C: Control Variables",                "main"),
    panel_row("&nbsp;&nbsp;Education Categories",          "sub"),
    row_dummy("Illiterate &mdash; No Schooling (ref)",     "edu_illiterate"),
    row_dummy("Primary &mdash; 1 to 5 years",              "edu_primary"),
    row_dummy("Middle &mdash; 6 to 8 years",               "edu_middle"),
    row_dummy("Secondary &mdash; 9 to 10 years",           "edu_secondary"),
    row_dummy("Higher Secondary &mdash; 11 to 12 years",   "edu_higher_sec"),
    row_dummy("Graduate and Above &mdash; 13 to 16 years", "edu_graduate"),
    panel_row("&nbsp;&nbsp;In-laws",                       "sub"),
    row_dummy("Father-in-law Alive (Yes = 1)",             "fil_alive"),
    row_dummy("Mother-in-law Alive (Yes = 1)",             "mil_alive")
  )
}
```

## Introduction {.center}

::::::: columns
:::: {.column width="52%"}

### Motivation {style="font-size: 1.3em;"}

::: {style="font-size: 1.15em; line-height: 2.0; margin-top: 20px;"}
- Women's employment is a key indicator of **empowerment** and household welfare
- Urban slum women face multiple barriers — family structure, marital status, and social norms
- Very few studies focus on determinants of employment among slum women in India
- This study uses data from **four urban slums** — Atal Ayub Nagar, Nawab Colony, J.P Nagar, Arif Nagar
:::
::::

:::: {.column width="48%"}

### Research Question {style="font-size: 1.3em;"}

::: {style="font-size: 1.1em; line-height: 1.9; background-color: #dceeff; padding: 25px; border-left: 6px solid #2c7fb8; border-radius: 6px; margin-top: 20px;"}
*"What determines women's employment in urban slums — role of marital status, family structure, and age?"*
:::

::: {style="font-size: 1.1em; line-height: 2.2; margin-top: 25px;"}
- **Dependent:** Currently Working (Yes/No)
- **Independent:** Marital Status, Family Type, Age
- **Controls:** Education, In-laws Alive
:::
::::
:::::::

---


## Data Cleaning {.center}

::: {style="font-size: 1.2em; line-height: 2.2; padding: 10px 60px; margin-top: 10px;"}
- Data collected from **four urban slums** in 2026

- Age = 0 replaced with **NA** &nbsp;— data entry error

- Education > 16 replaced with **NA** &nbsp;— beyond questionnaire range

- Marital status recoded: **Widowed / Separated = 1**, others = 0

- Education grouped into six categories: **Illiterate, Primary, Middle, Secondary, Higher Secondary, Graduate & Above**

- Age grouped into six categories: **18–24, 25–34, 35–44, 45–54, 55–64, 65+**

- **Binary dummies** created for each education and age category
:::

## Employment by Marital Status {.center}

```{r}
#| label: fig-marital
#| fig-cap: "Women's Employment Status by Marital Status"

W_SLUMS |>
  filter(!is.na(currently_working),
         !is.na(marital_status)) |>
  mutate(
    marital_lab = factor(
      case_when(
        marital_status == 1 ~ "Married",
        marital_status == 2 ~ "Unmarried",
        marital_status %in% c(3, 4) ~ "Widowed / Separated"),
      levels = c("Married",
                 "Unmarried",
                 "Widowed / Separated")),
    work_status = factor(
      if_else(currently_working == 1,
              "Working",
              "Not Working"),
      levels = c("Not Working", "Working"))
  ) |>
  
  count(marital_lab, work_status) |>
  group_by(marital_lab) |>
  mutate(
    pct = n / sum(n) * 100,
    lab = paste0(round(pct, 1), "%")
  ) |>
  
  ggplot(aes(marital_lab, pct,
             fill = work_status)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.5) +
  geom_text(aes(label = lab),
            position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5),
            size = 8,
            fontface = "bold") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    "Not Working" = "#F6DCDC",
    "Working" = "#00CC33"
  )) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = percent_format(scale = 1),
    limits = c(0, 100)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Figure 1: Women's Employment Status by Marital Status",
    x = "Marital Status",
    y = "% of Women",
    fill = NULL
  ) +
  
  theme_pres() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## Employment by Family Structure {.center}

```{r}
#| label: fig-family
#| fig-cap: "Women's Employment Status by Family Structure"

W_SLUMS |>
  filter(!is.na(currently_working),
         !is.na(joint_family)) |>
  mutate(
    family_lab = factor(
      joint_family,
      levels = c(0, 1),
      labels = c("Nuclear Family",
                 "Joint Family")),
    work_status = factor(
      if_else(currently_working == 1,
              "Working",
              "Not Working"),
      levels = c("Not Working", "Working")
    )
  ) |>
  
  count(family_lab, work_status) |>
  group_by(family_lab) |>
  mutate(
    pct = n / sum(n) * 100,
    lab = paste0(round(pct, 1), "%")
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(family_lab, pct,
             fill = work_status)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.5) +
  geom_text(aes(label = lab),
            position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5),
            size = 8,
            fontface = "bold") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    "Not Working" = "#F6DCDC",
    "Working" = "#00CC33"
  )) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = percent_format(scale = 1),
    limits = c(0, 100)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Figure 2: Women's Employment Status by Family Structure",
    x = "Family Type",
    y = "% of Women",
    fill = NULL
  ) +
  theme_pres() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## Employment by Age Group {.center}

```{r}
#| label: fig-age
#| fig-cap: "Women's Employment Status by Age Group"

W_SLUMS |>
  filter(!is.na(currently_working),

  mutate(
    age_lab = factor(
      age_group,
      levels = c(2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7),
      labels = c("18-24", "25-34", "35-44",
                 "45-54", "55-64", "65+")),
    work_status = factor(
      if_else(currently_working == 1,

    "Working" = "#00CC33"

  ) +
  labs(

    y = "% of Women",
```

## Key Findings {.center}

:::::: columns
::: {.column width="31%" style="font-size: 1.15em; line-height: 2.0; background-color: #dceeff; padding: 25px; border-radius: 10px; border-top: 5px solid #2c7fb8;"}
**📊 Marital Status**

- Married → **14.2%** working
- Unmarried → **25.0%** working
- Widowed / Separated → **41.7%** working
- Economic necessity drives work after loss of spouse
:::

::: {.column width="3%"}
:::

::: {.column width="31%" style="font-size: 1.15em; line-height: 2.0; background-color: #dceeff; padding: 25px; border-radius: 10px; border-top: 5px solid #2c7fb8;"}
**🏠 Family Structure**

- Nuclear family → **20.1%** working
- Joint family → **13.4%** working
- Joint families **restrict** women's mobility and work decisions
:::

::: {.column width="3%"}
:::

::: {.column width="31%" style="font-size: 1.15em; line-height: 2.0; background-color: #dceeff; padding: 25px; border-radius: 10px; border-top: 5px solid #2c7fb8;"}
**📅 Age & Education**
 
- Women aged **35–44** have highest employment (24.7%)
- More educated women work **less** — social restrictions in slum communities
:::
::::::
